messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Traffic spike + fallback-policy churn detected for customer-facing endpoints in eu-west-1. 5xx rate > 8% across 30s — auto-fallbacks triggered to variant-c-quant. Paging oncall.

alice: got the page. looking at routing dashboard now. seeing a big jump in fallback_count for policy `global-fallback-v2`.

oncall: I’m on it — collecting traces. can someone confirm which customers are on eu-west-1 reserved pools?

ben: quick note: we pushed a temporary policy yesterday to force-variant=fast-quant for perf tests. it should have been scoped to test-tenants only, but appears to have leaked to global. investigating.

mira: omg — that could explain why fallbacks are sticky. the variant is missing the compatible-kv-tag so runtime pins sessions.

oncall: can you paste the policy? I’m seeing a bunch of `force_variant` entries.

ben: here’s the patch we rolled: ```json
{"policy_name":"global-fallback-v2","rule":"force_variant:fast-quant","scope":"test-tenants,global?"}
``` looks like the scope was malformed and matched `*`.

raj: that matches the logs: ```
[2026-03-15T04:12:02Z] route-evaluator: matched rule id=842 force_variant=fast-quant scope=* tenant_id=customer-123
[2026-03-15T04:12:03Z] router: pinned shard to eu-west-1-quant-01 for session=abc123
```

oncall: ok decision time — do we remove the policy or try a rollback? removing is faster.

alice: if we remove immediately, some sessions might still be pinned. we should unset sticky flag and remove the force rule. plan:
1) remove `force_variant` from `global-fallback-v2`
2) run `redwoodctl routing unset-sticky --match variant=fast-quant --region=eu-west-1`
3) monitor 5xx and customer impact

mira: +1. also we should notify SRE to drain the affected pool to avoid serving degraded quant variant while clearing pins.

ben: executing step 1 now.

ben: done — removed `force_variant` from `global-fallback-v2`. config commit id = cfg_7782

oncall: running unset-sticky now: ```bash
redwoodctl routing unset-sticky --match variant=fast-quant --region=eu-west-1 --confirmed
``` returning 214 sessions cleared.

alice: starting drain on eu-west-1-quant-01: `redwoodctl pool drain --pool eu-west-1-quant-01 --timeout 120s` — starting.

incident-bot: ACTION: Postmortem ticket created: PM-2204. Notifying support to prepare customer-facing comms. cc: @support

mira: watching metrics — 5xx dropped from 8.3% -> 2.1% over 90s. P50 latency stable.

oncall: thanks. any sign of cascading fallback loops? I saw some repeated route-evaluator matches but they stopped after unset-sticky.

raj: logs show a loop earlier because the policy had both `force_variant` and a region fallback with `sticky=true`. once pinned, subsequent requests retried and re-pinned.

alice: important followup: we need a lint/check to prevent `scope` parsing falling back to wildcard when malformed. filing a tech-debt ticket.

ben: support asked for list of impacted tenants — I pulled: customer-123, customer-77, partner-x. sending to @support privately.

oncall: oncall -> handing off to mira for next 2 hours while I jump to another page. mira, please own monitoring and the postmortem draft.

mira: taking it. will keep the thread updated. immediate actions summary posted to #incidents-p0.

sre-bot: NOTE: Drain completed for eu-west-1-quant-01. All new allocations moved to eu-west-1-standard-02.

alice: verifying end-to-end: synthetic tests for top-10 flows passing. 5xx now 0.6%.

mira: preparing RCA outline: root cause = malformed policy scope + absence of scope validation; contributing factor = sticky fallback + variant incompatibility. mitigation = scope lint, disable sticky on fallbacks by default, post-deploy policy checks.

oncall: good. recommended immediate config change: default `sticky=false` for fallback policy rules and add `--validate-scope` to policy CLI.

ben: rolling a small hotfix to policy parser: `PR#4128` opened, will patch in next deploy window. including unit tests for scope parsing.

incident-bot: DECLARE: Severity=P2 (customer impact detected, mitigated). paging cleared. If anything else appears, re-open thread.

mira: I'll coordinate a short post-incident email for affected customers and attach the mitigation timeline. closing handoff to product for comms.

alice: one last note — we should run a one-hour retrospective with routing/serving/sg oncall to tighten runbooks. scheduling invite.

mira: thanks everyone. closing thread unless new findings. :thumbsup:
